key_insight: The paper argues that many video generation errors are not just model flaws, but a data imbalance problem: training videos rarely show enough viewpoint-driven geometry changes. By learning from geometry-aware supervision, the method aims to keep shapes, depth, and motion consistent when the camera moves.
problem_solved: It addresses geometric inconsistency in generated videos, where objects warp, parallax looks wrong, and camera motion can collapse into unnatural shot changes instead of smooth viewpoint transitions.
method: Identify the root cause: web-scale video data is dominated by moving objects under mostly static or weak camera motion, so viewpoint-change cues are scarce.
Introduce a geometry-focused learning strategy to better supervise how scenes should transform under camera motion.
Train the video model to preserve structure and appearance consistency across changing viewpoints, improving parallax and spatial coherence.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights that better video generation may require better supervision, not only bigger models. It is especially relevant for applications like filmmaking tools, virtual camera control, and 3D-consistent content generation.

paper_title: Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos
paper_authors: Weijie Lyu, Tiancheng Shen, Jason Li, Yujing Wang, Xiaoyuan Wang
